market_context: United States/general English; USDA freezer guidance for raw and cooked chicken at 0 °F/-18 °C
title: How long does chicken last in the freezer?

seo.title: How long does chicken last in the freezer?
seo.meta_description: At 0 °F, whole raw chicken keeps best quality up to 1 year, parts 9 months, ground chicken 3–4 months and cooked chicken about 4 months.
seo.search_intent: Find freezer storage times for whole, cut, ground and cooked chicken and understand quality versus safety.

excerpt: At 0 °F (-18 °C), USDA lists best-quality times of up to 1 year for whole raw chicken, 9 months for parts, 3–4 months for ground chicken and about 4 months for cooked leftovers. Continuously frozen chicken remains safe longer, but quality declines.
content_html:
Freezing stops bacterial growth, but it does not freeze food quality in place forever. At 0 °F (-18 °C) or below, the recommended month limits are primarily about flavor, texture and moisture rather than a sudden safety deadline.

USDA best-quality freezer times

Chicken productFreezer at 0 °F or below
Whole raw chickenUp to 1 year
Raw chicken partsUp to 9 months
Ground chicken or giblets3–4 months
Cooked chicken leftoversAbout 4 months
Cooked chicken casseroles, dishes or soup4–6 months
Cooked pieces covered with broth or gravyUp to 6 months

USDA notes that food kept continuously frozen remains safe indefinitely. The table tells you when quality is most likely to remain good.

Why whole chicken keeps quality longer

A whole bird has less exposed surface area relative to its mass. Ground chicken has dramatically more surface area exposed to oxygen, so oxidation and moisture loss become noticeable sooner. That helps explain the gap between one year for a whole bird and 3–4 months for ground chicken.

Packaging matters

Retail wrap is acceptable for short freezer storage, but it lets air through. For longer storage, overwrap the package or move chicken to a freezer bag or airtight container, pushing out as much air as practical. Less air means less dehydration and freezer burn.

Freezer burn is a quality problem

Pale, dry or leathery patches are caused by moisture loss. They do not automatically make chicken unsafe. If the food stayed frozen properly, affected areas can be trimmed after thawing, although flavor and texture may be poorer.

Freezing does not kill every bacterium

Many microorganisms survive freezing. Once chicken thaws, they can become active again, so thawed raw chicken must still be handled carefully and cooked to a safe internal temperature.

Safe thawing

Use the refrigerator, cold water with chicken sealed in a leak-proof bag, or the microwave. Chicken thawed in cold water or the microwave should be cooked promptly. Leaving raw poultry on the counter for hours is not a safe thawing method.

Freezer time is mainly a quality question once the chicken stays frozen

At a continuously frozen temperature of 0°F (-18°C) or below, properly handled chicken does not suddenly become unsafe when a calendar date passes. The recommended freezer times are primarily about keeping flavor and texture at their best. Whole birds generally keep quality longer than small pieces because they expose less cut surface to air, while cooked chicken and ground poultry tend to show quality changes sooner. That distinction matters: “best quality for nine months” is not the same statement as “dangerous on day 271.”

Packaging has a large effect on what the chicken is like when thawed. Supermarket overwrap is designed for retail display, not necessarily for many months in a freezer. For longer storage, adding a tight freezer bag, foil or other moisture-vapor-resistant wrap reduces air contact and surface drying. Removing excess air also limits oxidation. Label the package with the cut and freezing date before it disappears into a stack of identical frozen parcels.

Freezer burn appears as dry, pale or grayish patches where moisture has migrated from the surface. It is a quality defect rather than proof that pathogens grew while the meat remained frozen. The affected area can be tough or stale-tasting after cooking, so trimming it may improve the result. Strong rancid odors after thawing, leaking packages from a temperature-abuse episode or an uncertain history are different concerns and should not be dismissed as ordinary freezer burn.

Thawing method also determines whether a long-frozen package is handled safely at the end. Refrigerator thawing keeps the surface cold while the center softens. Cold-water thawing is faster but requires a leakproof package and regular water changes, and microwave-thawed chicken should be cooked promptly because parts may begin warming. Leaving chicken on the counter for hours allows the outer layers to enter warmer temperatures long before the center has thawed.

If the freezer loses power, time and temperature become more important than the original freezing date. Food that still contains ice crystals or has remained at refrigerator temperature can often be refrozen, although quality may decline. Chicken that has warmed for too long should not be judged safe by smell alone. A simple freezer thermometer and clearly dated packages make these decisions much easier than trying to reconstruct the history later.

Bottom line

Use one year for whole chicken, nine months for parts, 3–4 months for ground chicken and about four months for cooked chicken as practical quality targets. Date-labeling packages makes the freezer far easier to manage.

faq.question: Is chicken safe after a year in the freezer?
faq.answer: If it stayed continuously frozen at 0 °F or below, it can remain safe, but quality may be substantially lower. One year is USDA's best-quality guidance for a whole raw chicken.

faq.question: How long can chicken breasts stay frozen?
faq.answer: As raw chicken parts, the USDA best-quality guideline is up to 9 months.

faq.question: How long does cooked chicken last frozen?
faq.answer: Plain cooked chicken leftovers are best within about 4 months; some dishes with broth or gravy retain quality for 4–6 months.
